title: Build SRD source-region ledger coverage gate
description:
Implement a source-region ledger for the D&D 5e SRD importer audit artifacts. Repeated full audits keep finding new categories of missing prose after each targeted fix. The existing source-coverage artifact accounts well for headings, tables, stat blocks, and named records, but it can still hide prose-bearing regions behind broad statuses such as ignored:document-structure or ignored:record-group-heading. Recent examples included Variant rules, Equipment prose, Diseases/Poisons guidance, chapter/appendix intro prose, subclass overview prose, Magic Items A-Z, and Sample Traps.

Goal: enumerate every contiguous prose-bearing region in the vendored SRD PDF, not just table/stat-block/heading structures, and classify each region against generated records or explicit ignore reasons so missing prose is not discovered one category at a time.

The ledger should include regions such as chapter intro paragraphs; appendix intro paragraphs; prose under group headings; table prefaces and postfaces; prose between table rows and record entries; prose under subclass-family headings; prose under equipment/table group sections; prose before the first child record in a chapter/appendix; prose between adjacent generated record slices; and short one-paragraph explanations such as Magic Items A-Z and Sample Traps.

Each ledger entry should include at least: source page number or page range; heading path / source context; region type such as chapter-intro, appendix-intro, group-intro, record-body, table-preface, orphan-prose, or pure-structure; first source phrase; last source phrase; normalized body length or character count; classification such as record:<key>, child-of:<key>, intentionally-ignored:<reason>, pure-document-structure, or unrepresented; target record key when applicable; ignore reason when applicable; and confidence/guard notes when useful.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The audit bundle includes a machine-readable source-region ledger artifact, probably JSON, and optionally a readable markdown summary.
2. The ledger is generated deterministically from the vendored SRD PDF/text extraction.
3. The ledger distinguishes pure structural headings from headings that have body prose.
4. A generic ignored:document-structure or ignored:record-group-heading classification is not allowed for prose-bearing regions unless the ledger proves there is no body prose or provides a specific explicit ignore reason.
5. The audit fails if any prose-bearing region is classified as unrepresented.
6. The audit fails if any prose-bearing region is hidden behind a broad structural ignore without a specific reason.
7. Existing source-coverage artifact behavior can remain, but the new ledger must be strong enough to catch the categories missed by previous audits.
8. Tests include fixtures or SRD-slice examples for: a pure heading with no body prose; a chapter intro with prose before first child heading; a group heading with a short prose intro before records; a table heading with body prose and table rows; adjacent records with no orphan prose; and prose that should be intentionally ignored with an explicit reason.
9. Regression tests or sentinels cover previous missed classes: Variant rules; Equipment prose/item mechanics; Diseases/Poisons guidance; Feats intro; Conditions intro; Using Ability Scores intro; subclass-family overview prose; Appendix MM-A/MM-B intros; Magic Items A-Z; and Sample Traps.

Implementation guidance: prefer adding this as an audit artifact/gate rather than rewriting all parsers. The first version can be conservative and targeted if a fully generic PDF paragraph segmenter is too risky, but the model must be region-based rather than heading-only. Reuse existing page text / coordinate extraction where possible. Keep the ledger reviewable: concise first/last phrases are more useful than dumping entire prose bodies. Avoid brittle dependence on exact line wrapping when possible. Preserve deterministic behavior and source-hash/reproducibility guarantees. The ledger should help a human auditor answer: “What prose exists in the PDF, where did it go, and why is any of it ignored?”

Validation expected for implementation: focused unit tests for region extraction/classification; source-coverage/source-region artifact tests; generated audit bundle includes the new ledger; npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack; npm run audit-bundle:dnd5e-srd; npm run verify:worktree.

Out of scope: do not change record schemas unless needed and justified; do not import new SRD content as part of the ledger task unless a small sentinel fixture requires it; do not replace the existing source-coverage artifact wholesale unless that is clearly simpler and safe; do not use LLM reasoning as the source of truth because this must remain deterministic and reproducible.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic SRD source-region ledger artifact/gate, added audit-bundle and verifier integration, regenerated artifacts, added focused and committed-artifact tests, and imported the Spellcasting chapter intro exposed by the new gate.
